paragraphs.source_en: It was nearly the fourth quarter of the Hour of the Sheep when Chaya Shirōjirō left Shōan's residence. Ieyasu had ordered him to investigate conditions in the Kinai region, and his inquiries were nearly complete. His next plan was to go to Kyoto, then slip into Mikawa and carefully investigate every subsequent move made by Akechi Mitsuhide, the instigator of the present upheaval.

paragraphs.source_en: Six days had already passed since the outbreak of the disturbance. Having safely withdrawn to Okazaki, Ieyasu had assembled some eight thousand elite troops under Sakai Tadatsugu, who should now be on the road to Owari Province. They were not, of course, simply marching straight on Azuchi. Ieyasu meant to prevent the fighting from spreading farther east of Owari, while outwardly creating the impression that he could attack Mitsuhide at any moment and thereby holding Mitsuhide in check.
